calculation_handling.description: Scope: Article 10.80.40 applies to buildings and structures in the RM zone, except ancillary buildings or structures, which are governed by Article 10.5.60.
Where the zone label has a 'u' value, that value is the maximum number of dwelling units on the lot.
An apartment building on a lot abutting a major street may have the greater of 60 units or the label 'u' value.
calculation_handling.gaps: Apartment buildings are outside MaxBLD building types.

units.disclosure: An apartment building on a major street may have up to 60 units, or more if the zone label allows. We do not model apartment buildings, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Each townhouse dwelling unit must be at least 5.0 m wide where it has no individual private driveway leading directly to its front.
calculation_handling.gaps: The negative driveway condition cannot be expressed as a token; it is listed in application only. Width is per townhouse dwelling unit.

calculation_handling.description: Each townhouse dwelling unit must be at least 6.0 m wide in all other cases (i.e. where it has an individual private driveway to its front).
calculation_handling.gaps: Driveway layout is a design input.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets principal building requirements for a detached house, a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to them.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content; 'only residential building on a lot' has no vocabulary token.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets principal building requirements for a semi-detached house, a semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot is subject to them for the portion that is one dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Depends on the Chapter 900 exception content.

calculation_handling.description: Where a base regulation in 10.80.40.10 or 10.80.40.40 for a detached or semi-detached houseplex is more permissive than the exception-derived requirement under 10.80.40.1(4), the more permissive base regulation prevails.
calculation_handling.gaps: Ranking applies only to clauses 10.80.40.10 and 10.80.40.40 and the houseplex types.

calculation_handling.description: A two-unit houseplex may have at most four bedrooms per dwelling unit (8 in total).
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the proposed unit and bedroom counts.

calculation_handling.description: A houseplex with three or more units may have at most three bedrooms per dwelling unit.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs the proposed unit and bedroom counts.

calculation_handling.description: Counting rule: a bachelor dwelling unit counts as one bedroom for (A) and (B).
Transition: a lawfully existing houseplex may exceed the bedroom maximum in (6), provided no bedrooms are added after June 26, 2025 that would increase the non-compliance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs as-built bedroom counts and lawful-existing status.

units.disclosure: An existing houseplex built lawfully may keep more bedrooms than the current limit, as long as none are added after June 26, 2025. We cannot verify existing buildings, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: Transition: a houseplex built under a building permit issued after June 26, 2025 may exceed the bedroom maximum if it has no more bedrooms per unit than an approval (zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance or site plan) applied for on or before June 26, 2025.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs application and permit history we do not hold.

units.disclosure: Projects with planning approvals applied for on or before June 26, 2025 may keep their approved bedroom counts. We do not hold application history, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: For a building relying on the (B) transition, no bedrooms may be added after the permit if they would increase the non-compliance beyond what that permit established.
calculation_handling.gaps: Needs permit history and as-built bedroom counts.

units.disclosure: A building that relies on the bedroom transition rule may not add bedrooms beyond its permit. We do not hold permit history, so this is not evaluated.

calculation_handling.description: 'Lawful / lawfully existing' also covers buildings, structures or uses authorized or permitted on or before June 26, 2025 and for which a building permit was lawfully issued before that date. The text says 'For the purposes of regulation 10.80.40.1(8)' (a self-reference); read conservatively as supporting the transition rule in 10.80.40.1(7), matching the parallel 10.40.40.1(9).
calculation_handling.gaps: Apparent cross-reference defect in the source text (self-reference to (8)).

calculation_handling.description: Defines 'request for a zoning certificate' by reference to Municipal Code Chapter 363, Article I.
Defines 'complete application for a zoning by-law amendment' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.
Defines 'complete application for a minor variance' by reference to O. Reg. 200/96, Section 2.
Defines 'complete application for site plan approval' by reference to Official Plan Policy 5.5.2.

10.80.40.1(1).explanation: The building rules in Article 10.80.40 apply to buildings in the RM zone. Ancillary buildings such as garages and sheds follow Article 10.5.60 instead.

10.80.40.1(2).explanation: If the zone label on the map has a 'u' number, that is the maximum number of homes on the lot. An apartment building on a major street may have 60 units, or the 'u' number if that is higher.

10.80.40.1(3).explanation: In the RM zone, each townhouse unit must be at least 5.0 m wide if it has no private driveway to its front, and at least 6.0 m wide otherwise.

10.80.40.1(4).explanation: If a site-specific exception sets building rules for a detached or semi-detached house, the same rules apply to a detached or semi-detached houseplex that is the only home building on the lot.

10.80.40.1(5).explanation: Where the regular RM height or floor-area rules for a houseplex are more generous than the rules carried in from a site-specific exception, the more generous rules apply.

10.80.40.1(6).explanation: A houseplex in the RM zone may have up to four bedrooms per unit when it has two units, and up to three per unit when it has three or more. A bachelor unit counts as one bedroom.

10.80.40.1(7).explanation: An existing lawful houseplex, or one approved through an application filed on or before June 26, 2025, may keep more bedrooms than the limit. It may not add bedrooms that make the excess larger.

10.80.40.1(8).explanation: These definitions support the bedroom transition rule. They define 'lawfully existing' (authorized or permitted by June 26, 2025) and what counts as a complete application for a zoning certificate, rezoning, minor variance or site plan approval.
